title: But If Not: Daniel 3-4, Job 19, John 12, 2 John
summary: Daniel 3 was set with the Greek versions' 'eighteenth year' (about 586 B.C., uncertain) and read as Nebuchadnezzar's all-gold answer to the ch. 2 statue; the repeated lists were taught as the drone of empire with Matthew Henry quoted ('concert of music, or driven to by a fiery furnace'). On 3:17-18 'But if not' Keil's ethical-ability point was paraphrased (they doubted not God's power but his will) and Spurgeon No. 2217 (1891) quoted ('Theirs was not cupboard love'). Hard question one, the fourth man (bar elahin; 3:28 'his angel'): Calvin and Jerome (angel; Jerome's 'how an ungodly king could have merited') paraphrased, Poole and Gill (Christ), and Hippolytus quoted ('he found no name by which to call the fourth'); the host held the Angel of the Lord loosely and stressed Isaiah 43:2, with Hebrews 11:34 as the single NT move. Daniel 4 was taught as a royal letter: the tree, the watcher, the thesis stated three times (4:17, 25, 32), 4:27 'break off' against the Vulgate's 'redeem by alms' (Calvin, Poole, Ellicott), the roof speech set beside the East India House Inscription, and 4:34's lifted eyes (Jerome paraphrased). Hard question two, was Nebuchadnezzar converted: Henry (sure he was, paraphrased) vs Calvin quoted ('never truly converted') with Gill in between; the host leaned to Calvin's caution while keeping Henry's hope; application: what you say on your roof (Calvin paraphrased on pride slow to cure). Job 19 in four steps: siege, desertion, the inscription wish (Henry paraphrased: God granted it), go'el (Boaz, avenger of blood; God who seems an enemy called kin), 'in/without my flesh', Jerome quoted ('athlete of the Church'). John 12:37-50: could not vs would not (Chrysostom, Augustine, Calvin paraphrased), Isaiah saw Christ's glory with Sproul quoted ('The One Who Sent Me'), the doxa wordplay of 12:41/43 with J. C. Ryle quoted ('knowing too much of religion...'), and the last public words (Augustine paraphrased on mercy before judgment). 2 John was introduced and finished: the elder, the elect lady (Clement's Electa ruled out by v13; Poole), truth five times, love as obedience, Cerinthus, proagon 'go on ahead' (Cambridge paraphrased), vv10-11 as itinerant teachers (Henry paraphrased), and Irenaeus quoted on John fleeing the bath-house. Closing connection: glory (the glory of my majesty; the glory that comes from man; Isaiah saw Christ's glory; glory come in the flesh).
threads: Daniel 5-6 is next: Belshazzar's feast with the temple vessels (taken in 1:2), the writing on the wall (mene, mene, tekel, parsin), the queen recalling Daniel, Babylon's fall to the Medes and Persians (539 B.C.; Nabonidus/Belshazzar co-regency from the Nabonidus Chronicle), and Daniel in the lions' den under Darius the Mede (6:10 windows open toward Jerusalem; JFB pairs ch. 3 and 6). Calvin calcom24 continues from Lecture 22; Jerome's commentary (tertullian.org jerome_daniel_02_text.htm) continues; Hippolytus' Scholia (newadvent 0502) covers ch. 6. Daniel 5:21 recalls Nebuchadnezzar's madness, so ch. 4 can be referenced briefly.

Unused Daniel 3-4 material: Oppert's Dura mounds and the el-Mokhattat brick pedestal (Cambridge, Keil); Spurgeon No. 2217 'Thirteen times their names recur in this chapter', 'You have challenged God and God shall make His own reply', and the excuses ('Everybody else is doing it', 'It is only for once'); Calvin 'of what use is life except to serve God's glory?' and Cyprian's 'There can be no deliberation in a matter so sacred!'; Henry 'Turn, or burn' and 'God will deliver us, either from death or in death'; Ligonier 'Courage Under Fire' ('they did not owe the Lord service because of what He could do for them but because He alone is God'); Ligonier 'God Humbles Nebuchadnezzar' ('a man who thought himself a god was made a beast to learn that he was but a man'); Henry 'Nebuchadnezzar would be more than a man, but God justly makes him less than a man'; Spurgeon No. 949 'The Unconquerable King' (1870) on Daniel 4:34-35; Hippolytus on Daniel smiling from a distance; Jerome on Daniel grieving for the king; Poole 'crowing and pruning his gay feathers'.

Job 20 is next: Zophar's second speech, the triumph of the wicked is short (20:5), he swallows riches and vomits them (20:15). Job 21 will answer that the wicked often prosper. Unused Job 19: Gregory Moralia XIV on Eutychius pinching his own skin ('I confess that we shall all rise again in this flesh'); Calvin Sermon 72 (Golding 1574) 'he maketh the dust to awake out of hand'; Spurgeon No. 504 (1863) 'the Book of books embalms the words of Job' and the 'dismasted vessel'; Spurgeon No. 2909 'they can call him Lord, but not Redeemer'; Henry 'a resurrection of names, as well as bodies'; Clement of Rome 1 Clement 26; Lucas (Ligonier 'The North Star'); Ellicott on the burial office. Gregory's Moralia is now reachable only via archive.org (lectionarycentral blocks bots).

John 13:1-11 is next: the Upper Room begins the 'Book of Glory'; 'having loved his own... he loved them to the end', the devil and Judas, Jesus washing feet, Peter's refusal, 'If I do not wash you, you have no share with me', 'not every one of you is clean'. Unused 12:37-50: Augustine 53 'He foretold it, but did not cause it' and 54 'We believe an apostle, but we do not believe in him'; Chrysostom 68 'not because Isaiah spoke, that they believed not; but because they were not about to believe, that he spoke' and his reading that Isaiah saw the Father's glory; Calvin 'golden fetters' and 'approbation or ratification of the doctrine of the Gospel'; Westcott 'climax of unbelief'; the secret believers Nicodemus and Joseph (19:38-39) who confessed after the cross.

3 John is next: Gaius commended for hospitality to traveling brothers, Diotrephes 'who likes to put himself first' refusing them, Demetrius. It is the mirror of 2 John 10-11 (whom to receive vs whom to refuse); Sinclair Ferguson's 'Guidelines for Separation' (Ligonier) balances the two. Calvin wrote no commentary on 2 or 3 John (Owen's preface in calcom45), so do not cite one. Unused 2 John: Plummer 'such an advance is not progress but apostasy'; Henry 'Deniers of the faith are destroyers of souls'; Ligonier 'Truth and Love' ('if we abandon love, we do not know the truth'); MacArthur 63-1 'You also have to be afraid of who gets in the homes'; Polycarp to Marcion 'the first-born of Satan'.

Voices quoted this episode: Matthew Henry (Daniel 3:1-7 concise), C. H. Spurgeon (No. 2217, 'Three Names High on the Muster-Roll', 1891), Hippolytus (Scholia on Daniel 3:26), John Calvin (Lecture 16 on Daniel, 'never truly converted'), Jerome (Against John of Jerusalem 30, Job 19:25), R. C. Sproul ('The One Who Sent Me'), J. C. Ryle (Expository Thoughts on John 12:42-43), Irenaeus (Against Heresies 3.3.4). Paraphrased: Keil, Ellicott, Poole, Gill, Jerome (Commentary on Daniel 3-4), Calvin (Daniel 3:25, 4:27, 4:34; John 12:39), Henry (Daniel 4, Job 19, 2 John 10), Chrysostom (Homily 68), Augustine (Tractates 53-54), Clement of Alexandria (Adumbrations), Cambridge Bible (Plummer), East India House Inscription. Desiring God was not checked (blocked).

show_notes: Three young men refuse to bow to a ninety-foot golden image, and the proudest king on earth ends up eating grass until he looks up. Job declares, 'I know that my Redeemer lives,' John closes Jesus' public ministry with the glory Isaiah saw, and the short letter of 2 John warns against teachers who 'go on ahead' of Christ.
